one-check-per-line.why: all 6 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 6

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 6 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why:
Checks 1, 2, 3 and 5 test only what their expect lines say. Two checks go further than their lines:
- Check 4's line says only "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged". Its FAIL condition is "any diff in lint (or the file) shown", and its command diffs the whole file. That is a file-scope rule the words don't require: a comment changed elsewhere in src/index.js would fail it even if lint() is unchanged.
- Check 6's PASS requires "the PR is open on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test". The expect line only says the change is one PR on that repo. It never says the PR must be open, so a merged PR would fail a test the words don't require.
Both stricter conditions belong under Advisory, not in PASS or FAIL, so the criterion is not met.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. Each one names something that exists at this commit or is made earlier in the same command. Files that exist include packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, src/index.js, test/cli.test.js, README.md and .github/workflows/test.yml. The temp files are made by `mktemp -d` and `printf` inside the same command. The shell syntax is valid: `&&` chains, `; echo "exit=$?"`, `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, and single-quoted grep patterns such as `'`-`'`. `npm test -w packages/jsonl-lint` works because the root test script already uses `--workspaces`. `git diff --exit-code "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)" HEAD -- path` and the `gh api` REST calls with `--jq` are well-formed. The builder's `readFileSync(0, 'utf8')` and spawnSync `input` are valid Node. The only non-literal piece is `N=<PR number>`, and the brief marks it as a placeholder ("N = the PR number"), so it doesn't count against the criterion.

catches-traps.why:
I checked all four must_catch items against the briefs, and each one is handled.
(1) Verifier Check 3's second command runs `a.jsonl missing.jsonl b.jsonl`, where b.jsonl has a bad row. PASS requires the stderr error, "still prints `<T>/b.jsonl:2: ...`" and exit=2, so the combined case is tested, not each case alone.
(2) Check 4 runs `git diff --exit-code "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)" HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` and needs no diff. That compares the file at the PR head against the base.
(3) Builder step 6 says "Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md" and covers multi-file usage, `-`, and the exit codes.
(4) Check 6 uses gh api to read the PR body and head sha, then the check-runs at that sha. It requires the Closes line and the `test` check to be completed with conclusion success.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its expect line. The behaviour checks (1–3) all run the program, so must_not item 2 is avoided. Item 1 is broken in two places. Check 3 requires the second run to write "an error naming missing.jsonl to stderr", but line 3 only says "error on stderr". That adds a requirement on what stderr says, which is the "exact stderr wording" kind of strictness the must_not list rules out. Check 6 requires "the PR is open", but line 6 only asks for one PR with the Closes body and green checks at its head. Under check 6, a PR that was merged before verification would fail even though line 6 holds. Builder steps such as "Edit only … jsonl-lint.js" are instructions to the builder, not PASS conditions, so I did not count them.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with every check in the verifier brief. None of the verifier's probes appear in the builder brief. That covers its mktemp fixtures with specific inputs (e.g. '{"b":2}\n{oops}\n'), the piped `printf | node ... -` runs, the `git diff --exit-code` merge-base command, the README grep patterns and the gh api check-runs query. The builder brief also has no PASS/FAIL wording. It gives the bar: the six quoted expect lines plus implementation steps such as "If `-` appears more than once: usage error ... exit 2". Step 5 lists the cases and the expected behaviour for tests the builder writes itself, which the criterion allows. Step 7 tells it to run `npm test`, also allowed. Some lines overlap with verifier advisories ("byte-for-byte as before", "do not hang"). Those only restate requirements from expect line 1 and the usage-error rule. They are not checks or probes, and the advisories are not pass/fail anyway.
